name: Seaweed / kelp foods (nori, wakame, kombu, dulse — dried, as sold)

MeHg.control: Seaweed is a marine primary producer, not a predator; methylmercury does not biomagnify into algae, so MeHg is a negligible fraction of total mercury. Bounded by the tHg cell (Israel dried-seaweed tHg 2500): if tHg passes, MeHg is inherently far below any fish MeHg action level.
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen (EPA 7473 / ICP-MS); reflex MeHg speciation (GC-ICP-MS, e.g. EPA 3200 / DIN EN 16801) only on a tHg exceedance.

Sn.control: Tin is a can-migration analyte, not a matrix-accumulation analyte. Dried seaweed foods (nori, wakame, kombu, dulse) are sold in non-metal packaging; with no tinplate contact there is no tin source. Every government tin ML in the register is either canned-product-only or an 'any food' catch-all set for can migration.
Sn.reference_method: Packaging control (non-tinplate); periodic ICP-MS tin verification on finished product.

Al.label: Conservative finished-food read-across from the AU-NZ infant-formula aluminium maximum (500 ug/kg). No sovereign seafood-specific aluminium maximum is loaded; total Al remains tested and this transfer is disclosed rather than derived from occurrence data.
Al.basis_note: face value (nearest government value; comparator vs any direct limit)

Cr.label: India FSSAI total-chromium maximum for all fishery products (12000 ug/kg); directly applicable to fishery rows and used as the nearest sovereign marine-food read-across for seaweed.
Cr.basis_note: face value (nearest government value; comparator vs any direct limit)

Cr-VI.control: Total chromium is measured on every lot. Any total-Cr result at or above 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails certification.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS; Cr(VI) by EPA 3060A alkaline extraction with IC-ICP-MS (EPA 6800 / EN 15192 or equivalent).

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default, 8:1 basis, read-across)
